headline: Animal feed and palm oil drive growth; crop protection/dairy muted due to weak monsoon

highlights: Revenue grew 17% YoY to INR 30bn, driven by animal feed, vegetable oil and B2C foods, while EBITDA margin contracted to 6.7% on weakness in crop protection and dairy.
Animal feed EBIT rose 32% YoY, and vegetable oil volumes (FFB +14% YoY) stayed strong, with the PKO derivatives plant commissioned on 1 Sep’26.
Management retains double-digit FFB volume growth guidance for FY27/FY28.
Crop protection, Astec and dairy are likely to stay under pressure in the near term, while Godrej Foods (B2C +50% YoY) and the ACI Godrej Bangladesh JV are emerging as growth drivers.
valuation: Initial commercialisation has started, with meaningful contribution over the next 2–3 years and a medium-term target of 50–55% CDMO share.

The innovation-led diversification continues to progress: Ashitaka (maize herbicide) delivered first-year revenue of over INR 1bn, TAKAI insecticide has been launched for multiple crops, and Ghassnash (soybean herbicide) was launched in Nov’26.

Management targets annual OER of at least 19.7%, aiming to recover the weather- related shortfall, and retains double-digit FFB growth guidance for FY27/FY28, supported by maturing and younger plantations.
watch: A 40% rainfall deficit in Jun’26 affected cotton sowing, and Aug–Oct’26 remained challenging across key agricultural markets.

Over the medium term, the company plans to introduce 1– 2 new products annually and expand into seven crop segments by FY29–30, reducing dependence on cotton and chilli, with field activation, distribution expansion and brand building as key priorities.
